extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, engineers, and members of scientific/engineering societies)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and conditions for submitting a paper to the Institution of Mechanical Engineers' 'Water Arbitration Prize' (engineering prize essay competition), including topic, eligibility, formatting, originality, and handling/publication rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize topic
rubrics_metrics.description: The award will be made to the author of the selected paper dealing with the filtration and purification of water for public supply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prize is to be offered for a paper on an engineering subject to be announced by the council one year before the time for sending in the papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to compete
rubrics_metrics.description: Members, associate members, associates, and graduates of the institution may compete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only those classes of persons are explicitly allowed to enter this competition (others are not stated as eligible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission address and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be sent in to the secretary of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, and must reach him not later than January 3, 1908.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure physical delivery to the secretary by the stated date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript presentation (page and typing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper must be clearly written, or typewritten, on one side only of foolscap paper, with a margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legibility and conventional margins are required; single-sided foolscap format is mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synopsis/abstract requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper must be accompanied by an outline or synopsis of its contents of not more than six hundred words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise synopsis (≤600 words) is a compulsory part of the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Any illustrations submitted with the paper must be properly drawn to scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures/diagrams must be prepared to scale and presented professionally; no further illustration format details given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership and disposition of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted for competition will become the property of the institution, and, at the discretion of the council, may be either read and discussed at a general meeting or printed in the Proceedings without having been so read and discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors surrender ownership to the institution upon submission; the council has discretion over reading/printing. Any paper not accepted for printing will be returned to the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and authorship declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper must consist of original matter written by the competitor himself, and the council will require a written statement to that effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must provide a written declaration of authorship/originality confirming the work is their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: No paper which has been previously published will be accepted for competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be unpublished original work; previously published material is ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award form and insufficient merit policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize will take any form which the council may from time to time decide upon, and will be accompanied by a certificate bearing the seal of the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, in the opinion of the council, no paper of sufficient merit be received in reply to any particular offer of the prize, the amount available for that award will be added to the capital of the fund.
